classification.difficultyReason: Represent related rectangle dimensions algebraically, form an area equation and reject a negative solution.

content.prompt:
The solutions to most of the practical problems should begin with a diagram.

A rectangular paddock is 50 m longer than it is wide. If the area of the paddock is $10\,400\text{ m}^2$, find its dimensions.

answer.worked:
Let the width be $x$ m, so the length is $(x+50)$ m, where $x>0$.
$$\begin{align*}x(x+50)&=10\,400\\x^2+50x-10\,400&=0\\(x+130)(x-80)&=0\\x&=-130\text{ or }80\end{align*}$$
Reject $x=-130$ because a length must be positive. The width is $80\text{ m}$ and the length is $80+50=130\text{ m}$.

Check: $80\times130=10\,400\text{ m}^2$.

spec.description: Authored unshaded rectangle illustrating the width and the length, which is 50 m greater.
spec.mathematics: Width x metres; length x+50 metres; x>0.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; students construct their own diagram.
